correctness.rationale: Fresh endpoint-reduced integer enumeration independently gives unique reduced optima (1,6,6,0,36,0,216,0,1296,0), (1,7,7,0,49,0,343,0,2401,0), and (2,7,12,2,88,0,640,0,4656,0) with values 7776, 16807 and 33872. The affine x5 coefficient is strictly positive at all three winning prefixes, and the x4 coefficient is also strictly positive there, so no omitted interior split ties the optimum. Proposition 11 of the primary paper applies because q>2 and gives counts 14, 16 and 6552; for q=9 one orientation has C(9,2)C(14,12)=3276 choices and reversal doubles it. The primary paper explicitly states that under its Proposition-11 hypotheses no code is double counted.

evidence: The primary paper is broader in q and n conceptually but publishes exact nonbinary cells only through q=6.
Blackburn's construction gives the q=7,8 optima but is 258 below the q=9 optimum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General frameworks/constructions do not imply the three exact frontier cells or their full maximum-code census.

A later same-repository record repeats only the three S-values, but repository history shows the present stronger record was imported first and is its ancestor, so that later duplicate does not negate priority.

final_claim: For length-six non-overlapping codes, S(7,6)=7776 with 14 maxima, S(8,6)=16807 with 16 maxima, and S(9,6)=33872 with 6552 maxima; q=7,8 maxima are the one-boundary AB^5 family up to reversal, while every q=9 maximum has the stated two-level partition profile up to reversal.
limitations: Only length six and q in {7,8,9} are classified.
